tossups.question: The narrator of this novel rents a cottage next to a mansion whose guests gossip that their host once killed a man. A green light at the end of a dock (*) transfixes this novel's title character, who longs for Daisy Buchanan. For 10 points, name this Jazz Age novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald.

This ruler crushed a combined Austrian and Russian army at Austerlitz. After a disastrous invasion of (*) Russia, this ruler abdicated and was exiled to Elba, returning for a Hundred Days that ended at Waterloo. For 10 points, name this French emperor.

The second law of thermodynamics states that this quantity never decreases in an isolated system. Ludwig Boltzmann related it to the (*) number of microstates through a logarithm. For 10 points, name this quantity symbolized S, a measure of disorder.

This novel's title character is locked in the red-room as a child at Gateshead and later teaches at Lowood School. She flees (*) Thornfield Hall after learning her employer keeps his wife Bertha Mason in the attic. For 10 points, name this Charlotte Bronte novel about a governess who loves Mr. Rochester.

Robert Livingston and James Monroe negotiated this transaction, prompted in part by the Haitian Revolution. It roughly (*) doubled the size of the United States for fifteen million dollars. For 10 points, name this 1803 deal in which Thomas Jefferson bought territory from France.

The light-dependent reactions of this process split water molecules to generate ATP and NADPH. Its dark reactions fix (*) carbon dioxide in the Calvin cycle. For 10 points, name this process by which chloroplasts in green plants turn sunlight into sugar.

A cypress tree rises like a dark flame on the left side of this painting, whose village church spire the artist added from (*) memory while at an asylum in Saint-Remy. For 10 points, name this swirling nighttime scene by Vincent van Gogh.

During this observance, a pre-dawn meal called suhoor precedes daily abstention from food and drink. Its end is celebrated at (*) Eid al-Fitr, and the Quran was first revealed during it on the Night of Power. For 10 points, name this Islamic holy month of fasting.

This river passes through the Iron Gates gorge on the border of Serbia and Romania. Rising in Germany's (*) Black Forest, it flows through more national capitals than any other river, including Vienna and Budapest. For 10 points, name this second-longest river of Europe.

A recurring item in this video game series is the Master Sword, often drawn from a pedestal deep in a forest. Its protagonist collects pieces of the (*) Triforce and rescues a princess of Hyrule from Ganon. For 10 points, name this Nintendo series starring Link.

bonuses.leadin: The Buendia family founds the town of Macondo in this author's most famous novel. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Colombian author of One Hundred Years of Solitude.
Garcia Marquez wrote in this literary style, which weaves fantastical events into otherwise ordinary settings.
In this Garcia Marquez novel, Florentino Ariza waits more than fifty years to reunite with Fermina Daza.

bonuses.leadin: This city's traditional founding date is 753 BC. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this city, ruled by seven legendary kings before it became a republic.
This first Roman emperor defeated Antony and Cleopatra at Actium.
Augustus's rise ended decades of civil war that began when this general crossed the Rubicon.

bonuses.leadin: These elements make up group 18 of the periodic table. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this family of largely unreactive elements.
This lightest noble gas is the second-most abundant element in the universe.
This noble gas glows reddish-orange in signs and lends its name to them.

bonuses.leadin: Three witches greet this character as Thane of Cawdor and king hereafter. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this Scottish general who murders King Duncan in his namesake Shakespeare tragedy.
Macbeth is finally slain by this nobleman, who was from his mother's womb untimely ripped.
This wife of Macbeth sleepwalks while trying to wash imagined blood from her hands.

bonuses.leadin: A Parisian crowd stormed the Bastille on July 14, 1789. For 10 points each:
parts: The Bastille's fall began this revolution, which overthrew the Bourbon monarchy.
This radical Jacobin leader dominated the Committee of Public Safety during the Reign of Terror.
This king was executed by guillotine in January 1793.

bonuses.leadin: This planet's Great Red Spot is a storm that has raged for centuries. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this largest planet in the solar system.
This Galilean moon of Jupiter is the most volcanically active body in the solar system.
Io and Jupiter's other large moons were discovered in 1610 by this Italian astronomer.

bonuses.leadin: A critic coined this movement's name from a painting of a sunrise over Le Havre. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this nineteenth-century French movement that captured fleeting effects of light.
This Impressionist painted Impression, Sunrise as well as a series of water lilies at Giverny.
This Impressionist is known for paintings of ballet dancers such as The Dance Class.

bonuses.leadin: This religion's Trimurti consists of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this major religion of India.
This Hindu concept names the cycle of death and rebirth.
This dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna forms part of the Mahabharata.

bonuses.leadin: This continent's highest peak is Kilimanjaro. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this continent.
This longest river of Africa flows north through Egypt to the Mediterranean.
This Ethiopian capital hosts the headquarters of the African Union.

bonuses.leadin: This studio's films open with a hopping desk lamp. For 10 points each:
parts: Name this animation studio behind Toy Story.
In this Pixar film, the rat Remy cooks in a Paris restaurant.
This Pixar film about personified emotions takes place largely inside the mind of a girl named Riley.
